correctness.rationale: The dissipativity identity \(\operatorname{Im}\lambda\,\|u\|^2=-\gamma|u_0|^2/2\) and distinct real leaf energies force every eigenvalue strictly into the lower half-plane for nonzero disorder. The characteristic polynomial gives \(g^2P'(z)=\varepsilon(i\gamma/2+\varepsilon z)P(z)\), with \(\lambda=\varepsilon z\). For each simple interlacing root \(\theta\) of \(P'\), implicit differentiation and \(-P''(\theta)/P(\theta)=S\) give \(\lambda=\varepsilon\theta-i\gamma\varepsilon^2/(2g^2S)+O(\varepsilon^3)\). The normalized eigenvectors converge to an explicitly orthonormal basis \(|d_j\rangle\) of the dark sector, with mutually orthogonal limiting Riesz projections. The two complementary lossy eigenmodes decay on the \(\varepsilon^{-2}\) timescale even at their possible exceptional point. Trace cross-terms vanish; therefore every initial density matrix has the exact scaled survival limit \(\sum_j\exp[-\gamma\tau/(g^2S_j)]\langle d_j|\rho|d_j\rangle\). The proof applies at fixed parameters and \(\tau>0\). Independent finite-matrix construction checked eight parameter/epsilon pairs and 64 propagator comparisons as corroboration, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: Earlier spectral-transport/Krylov work characterizes bright subspaces but does not evaluate the disorder-induced relaxation rates for this model. Prior weak-disorder trapping studies on two-generation extended stars report complete eventual capture and very long-lived states, but the inspected formulae/discussion do not specify the critical-point-indexed multi-exponential limit for all initial density matrices on the one-generation star. The mathematical tools of secular determinants and perturbation theory are standard; the claim evaluated here is their exact physical rate formula and scaling limit. value.rationale: Disorder-enhanced absorption is qualitatively established, but weak disorder creates arbitrarily long-lived remnants: a physically central quantitative question is their characteristic timescale and distribution of relaxation rates. This theorem gives the complete nontrivial \(\varepsilon^{-2}\) survival profile for any initial state, \(k-1\) analytic modes, and explicit positive rates determined by all leaf detunings through real polynomial critical points. It converts previously numerical slow-capture behavior into a structural, reproducible asymptotic law and distinguishes configurations with the same variance. It is not just a restatement of eventual capture, an arbitrary finite table, or an unmotivated parameter slice. The claimed value is limited to the finite single-layer ideal star; no broader engineering performance guarantee is asserted.
